questions.question: Which 3 product categories generate the most revenue from completed orders?
questions.sql: SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS revenue FROM v_order_items AS oi JOIN v_orders AS o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN v_products AS p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 3
questions.assumptions: Revenue is SUM(quantity * unit_price) from order items, using the unit_price recorded on each order item, restricted to orders with status 'completed'. Ties at the third position are broken arbitrarily by LIMIT 3.
questions.answer: Returned 3 row(s) with columns category, revenue.

questions.question: What is the average order total for completed orders?
questions.sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(order_total) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_order_total FROM v_order_totals WHERE status = 'completed'
questions.assumptions: Uses v_order_totals, where order_total is the sum of quantity*unit_price per order, filtered to status = 'completed'. The average is rounded to 2 decimal places.

questions.question: How many customers signed up in each city?
questions.sql: SELECT city, COUNT(customer_id) AS customer_count FROM v_customers GROUP BY city ORDER BY customer_count DESC, city
questions.assumptions: Every row in v_customers is a customer who signed up, so counting customers per city gives sign-ups by city across all time. Customers with a NULL city are grouped together as a single NULL group.
questions.answer: Returned 8 row(s) with columns city, customer_count.

questions.question: Who are the 5 customers with the highest total completed order value?
questions.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(t.order_total) AS total_completed_order_value FROM v_order_totals AS t JOIN v_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE t.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY total_completed_order_value DESC, c.customer_id LIMIT 5
questions.assumptions: Only orders with status 'completed' are counted, and order value is the sum of order_total from v_order_totals per customer. Ties are broken by customer_id.
questions.answer: Returned 5 row(s) with columns customer_id, first_name, last_name, total_completed_order_value.

questions.question: What is the average unit price of products in each category?
questions.sql: SELECT category, ROUND(CAST(AVG(unit_price) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_unit_price FROM v_products GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
questions.assumptions: Uses the catalog unit_price in v_products (not the price at order time in v_order_items), averaged per category and rounded to 2 decimals.
questions.answer: Returned 4 row(s) with columns category, avg_unit_price.

questions.question: How many distinct products have been ordered at least once?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS distinct_products_ordered FROM v_order_items
questions.assumptions: Any product appearing on at least one order line counts as ordered, regardless of order status (including cancelled or returned orders).

questions.question: What fraction of orders are returned rather than completed?
questions.sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN status = 'returned' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS DECIMAL), 4) AS returned_fraction FROM v_orders WHERE status IN ('completed', 'returned')
questions.assumptions: Interpreted as returned orders divided by (completed + returned) orders, so cancelled orders are excluded from the denominator. The result is a fraction between 0 and 1, rounded to 4 decimals.

questions.question: How many orders has each customer placed, for customers with more than 3 orders?
questions.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM v_customers AS c JOIN v_orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 3 ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.customer_id
questions.assumptions: All orders are counted regardless of status (completed, cancelled, or returned). Only customers with more than 3 orders are included.
questions.answer: Returned 189 row(s) with columns customer_id, first_name, last_name, order_count.

questions.question: How many orders were placed in each status (completed, cancelled, returned)?
questions.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM v_orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY status
questions.assumptions: Counts every row in v_orders grouped by its status value; statuses with zero orders will not appear in the output.
questions.answer: Returned 3 row(s) with columns status, order_count.

questions.question: What is the average number of items per order?
questions.sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(quantity) AS DECIMAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 2) AS avg_items_per_order FROM v_order_items
questions.assumptions: Items are counted as total units (sum of quantity) per order, averaged across all orders that have at least one line item, regardless of status (completed, cancelled, or returned).
